first.rationale: Activation is down 6% QoQ—the most direct signal. memory_91 demonstrated that in-product activation messaging improved week-one engagement, and this levers existing product infrastructure without the retention risk flagged in memory_73 (promotional pricing). memory_31 and memory_86 show onboarding improvements drive adoption, but the 4% onboarding completion decline may be a leading indicator of deeper activation friction that messaging can address more safely. Promotional pricing is ruled out due to memory_73's documented 30-day retention cliff, which contradicts the primary objective of sustainable long-term revenue. Referral incentives (memory_57) are effective but drive secondary growth from existing customers, not the core activation shortfall. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is narrower in scope and doesn't address the SMB segment being pressured by competitor pricing. Activation messaging offers immediate diagnostic value on whether the problem is product clarity vs. deeper onboarding design, and it scales with low execution risk. Verification of memory_91 and memory_86 will confirm the magnitude of prior impact and whether seasonal or cohort effects might apply.
